item.title: Asteroid 2017 XD passes by
item.description:
18.09.2026, 16:41 UTC

An asteroid with an estimated diameter of 897–2,005 m will pass Earth at 48.01 million km, or 124.9 times the Earth–Moon distance, travelling at 37.1 km/s. For scale: an object of this scale is a heavyweight in the catalogue of near-Earth asteroids. This is not a close encounter – it makes the list as one of the largest objects passing us this week. The pass is entirely safe – approaches like this happen regularly and are tracked as a matter of routine.

Object record in the JPL database

item.title: Draconids meteor shower peak
item.description:
08.10.2027, 02:00 UTC

An unpredictable shower: usually weak, but a few times in history it has produced genuine meteor storms. The radiant is already high in the early evening. At maximum, up to 10 meteors per hour in theory (the ZHR – under a perfectly dark sky with the radiant overhead; in practice usually several times fewer). The radiant lies in Draco. A Moon 56% illuminated will brighten the sky a little. No equipment needed – just a reclining chair, warm clothes and a spot away from city lights.

item.title: Perseids meteor shower peak
item.description:
12.08.2027, 02:00 UTC

The most popular shower of the year – it falls in the holiday season and on warm nights. Its source is comet 109P/Swift-Tuttle. At maximum, up to 100 meteors per hour in theory (the ZHR – under a perfectly dark sky with the radiant overhead; in practice usually several times fewer). The radiant lies in Perseus. Unfortunately the Moon will be 77% illuminated and will drown out the fainter meteors – it is worth observing after it sets. No equipment needed – just a reclining chair, warm clothes and a spot away from city lights.

item.title: Total solar eclipse – the longest of the century
item.description:
02.08.2027, 10:07 UTC

Totality lasts 6 minutes and 23 seconds – the longest eclipse visible from land in the 21st century and indeed until 2114. The path runs across southern Spain and North Africa, passing over Luxor among other places. WARNING: never look at the Sun without certified solar filters – sunglasses or exposed film do NOT protect your eyes.
